chapter: Johnny Bayersdorffer band and early drummers
title: Zutty Singleton, the borrowed cymbal and the two drummers called Happy
summary: He tells of Zutty at the Lyric, a Zildjian cymbal, their friendship, and which Happy drummer was meant.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: He's the guy, he played in the pit that too. Oh, yeah? And Zutty played, Zutty played, played drums with that, and Happy played first drums with the, with the band. And Zutty, that story, the story brings me back. I was working, working there, helping, helping, uh, Howard Boris. He was selling the musical instrument with that Whirline music store, see? Mm-hmm. And, uh, I found a Zildjian symbol that I wanted to, wanted to keep. So I put it in, in one of the bottom drawers. Mm-hmm. And I, and I, uh, told Zutty about it. So he went into one day, I went to lunch, and he went in there, told him his Boris there, and there's a simul on at the bottom there, right foot away from it. And he took it, bought the goddamn thing. Oh, no. So I used, I used to go over, over, over to, over to the lyric, and, and say, Zutty, let me that simul, because I got to play an early job tomorrow, and I want, I want the right kind of sound, you know?

So he'd let me the simul, and I'd bring it back to him so he could make the show. Yeah. But Zutty, Zutty, we had a, we had a bar, we just loved each other, cause I used to go on the boat on Sundays, and, and, and go up on the roof, and I'd get a chick that had a basket, see, they used to go to St. Rose, they'd go out to St. Rose, and everybody went out on, in St. Rose, and had the basket lunch with them, see? But I used to go upstairs on the roof, so I'd find a chick that's got the right kind of bucket and stuff, so we'd go up on the roof and have Zutty share it with us. Oh, yeah.
We used to have a ball, it was wonderful. And, and which happy was that, was that red happy or black happy?
No, no, he was a colored guy.
Yeah, but you remember the, the real dark happy that was with Celestan in 1950, not that guy?

No, not that guy. Not that happy? No, no, no, this was a light-head guy. Yeah. And he was a, he was a fancy drummer, did a lot of stick work and stuff like that, see? Mm-hmm. But he, but he played, played the right kind of a beat, you know? Mm-hmm.
